description: No dedicated, standalone English-language IR portal was found for GRÁNIT Bank Nyrt.; the confirmed IR tree at granitbank.hu/befektetoknek is Hungarian-only in the sections observed.

result.result_summary: Hungarian searches returned a full HU IR structure; no en/ equivalent path surfaced in either HU or EN searching.

why_it_matters: Any Gránit monitoring must run on Hungarian-language parsing; English-only pipelines would silently miss Hungary's newest listed bank.

description: MBH Bank's disclosure estate is split across at least four hosts (mbhbank.hu, mbhbank.com, mbhbefektetesibank.hu, mbhjelzalogbank.hu) and still carries legacy 'mkb-bankrol' URL segments from the pre-merger entities.

result.result_summary: Documents for a single issuer group were found on four distinct domains during this pass.

why_it_matters: A single-domain crawler will under-collect MBH badly; the collection config must enumerate all four hosts and tolerate legacy paths.

description: MBH Bank's annual report is distributed as a digitally signed ZIP (ESEF-style) rather than a plain PDF, and MNB has issued a vezetői körlevél on ESEF/APM reporting for issuers.

result.result_summary: Search result text explicitly describes the annual report as available in digitally signed zip format.

why_it_matters: Text extraction must unpack ZIP/iXBRL packages; a PDF-only parser will register these filings as missing.

description: No K&H Jelzálogbank investor/disclosure estate could be located; Hungarian searches returned Erste and UniCredit mortgage-bank pages but nothing substantive for K&H.

result.result_summary: Hungarian query naming K&H Jelzálogbank produced no K&H-specific disclosure page.

why_it_matters: Either the entity does not exist under that name or it does not issue publicly; must not be assumed present in the issuer universe without confirmation.

description: All URLs in this slice come from search results, issuer document links, or (for granitbank.hu/befektetoknek) a single successful page read. Liveness of the remainder was not tested and is left to the deterministic verification pass.

result.result_summary: One page fetched successfully; no URL here is claimed as verified.

why_it_matters: Prevents false confidence; deep static-file paths on issuer sites in particular rotate between prospectus vintages.

description: WebFetch of the K&H disclosure hub https://www.kh.hu/csoport/nyilvanossagra-hozando-informaciok returned HTTP 403 Forbidden.

result.result_summary: Page is indexed by search engines with a coherent title and description, so it is almost certainly live and public; the 403 is bot defence at the edge, not absence. Recorded as a hypothesis, not a dead source.

why_it_matters: The collection pipeline for kh.hu must use a browser-class fetcher with a realistic user agent, or fall back to the MNB közzétételek mirror, otherwise K&H — a systemic bank — silently drops out of coverage.

description: No dedicated 'nyilvánosságra hozatal' / Pillar 3 page was found for Cofidis Magyarországi Fióktelepe on cofidis.hu, in either Hungarian or English searching.

result.result_summary: Only dated üzletszabályzat and adatkezelési tájékoztató PDFs under /media/ surfaced. Consistent with the EU-branch model: prudential disclosure sits with the French parent (Cofidis SA / Groupe Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale), not the Hungarian branch.

why_it_matters: Entity-level Hungarian numbers for Cofidis must be pulled from e-beszámoló or a commercial register vendor; expecting a self-published report will produce a false coverage gap.

description: Oberbank AG Magyarországi Fióktelep publishes no standalone Hungarian annual report on oberbank.hu; only Hitpt. 122.§(4)b) notices, MNB decisions and product terms were located.

result.result_summary: Search surfaced impresszum, hírek and product-terms PDFs, plus register entries showing filings made to the Ministry of Justice. No 'éves beszámoló' page on the bank's own domain.

why_it_matters: Confirms that branch-model institutions (fióktelep) have a materially thinner disclosure estate than Zrt.-model subsidiaries, and that register-based collection is mandatory for them.

description: For UniCredit Bank Hungary and CIB Bank, individual disclosure PDFs were located but no stable HTML index page for the disclosure series was confirmed within this run.

result.result_summary: UniCredit PDFs consistently sit under /content/dam/cee2020-pws-hu/Rolunk/befektetok/; CIB accounts under /document/publications/CIB/<year>/kozlemeny/ and /document/documents/CIB/kommunikacio/evesjelentesek/. Index URLs are inferred from those paths, not observed.

why_it_matters: A collector keyed to a guessed index URL will break; these two should be collected by DAM-path crawling or per-year site: queries until a real index is verified.

description: English-language equivalents of these statutory pages were largely absent; the disclosure estate for this cell is Hungarian-first.

result.result_summary: Search results for the cell were overwhelmingly hu-language; the only English-adjacent artefacts found were an English-labelled BÉT results_report path for CIB and English company-register pages. No bank in the cell surfaced a full English Pillar 3 / annual report index.

why_it_matters: Any English-only collection or query strategy for Hungarian foreign-owned subsidiaries will under-collect severely; hu-language terms are load-bearing, not a nice-to-have.

description: Searched for an AmCham Hungary financial-services committee roster in English. Results returned only individual member company profile pages (OTP, K&H, ING branch, Deutsche Bank branch) and the general Board of Directors page; no committee membership page surfaced.

result.result_summary: Committee-level membership for AmCham's financial services work is not visible in search results; only company-level directory entries and the Board page were found.

why_it_matters: Committee rosters would name the specific executives shaping the sector agenda; without them, AmCham is usable as a company register but not as a decision-maker map.

description: The Magyar Bankszövetség /jelentesek page shows numbered annual reports for 2001–2018 and quarterly reports for 2011–2018, while separate 'Egyszerűsített Éves Beszámoló' filings exist for 2023–2025. No 2019–2022 annual sector report was observed on that page.

result.result_summary: An apparent gap in the association's published annual/quarterly sector report series after 2018; recent years are represented only by simplified statutory accounts.

why_it_matters: If the periodic sector report genuinely stopped, sector-level narrative for 2019+ must be reconstructed from Kommunikék, Publikációk and press releases instead — a materially different collection design.

description: The Magyar Fintech Szövetség (MAFISZ/HFA) member roster at hunfintech.com/hu/tagok/ was identified as the correct URL via site navigation, but the enumerated list of member companies was not returned in the fetched content — only founding members (Bankmonitor, Barion, BÁV Faktor, Blueopes, Flexibill, Péntech, Rocketsheperd, Tőkeportál, TechTeamer, dr. Vida Mariann Ügyvédi Iroda, MKB Fintechlab as supporting member) and current board affiliations (Ergománia, Tőkeportál, HOLD Alapkezelő, Barion, BlockBen) were observable.

result.result_summary: Member page located but roster content not extracted in this pass; likely JS-rendered.

why_it_matters: This is the highest-value fintech register in the cell; a rendered-DOM fetch is needed before the ecosystem can be enumerated.

description: Across the hu-language searches run for this cell, no distinct Hungarian payment-service-provider or acquirer association (an equivalent of a 'Magyar Pénzforgalmi Szövetség' or a PSP/e-money trade body) surfaced. Payments interests appear to be represented inside the Magyar Bankszövetség, the Magyar Fintech Szövetség and IVSZ's fintech working group instead.

result.result_summary: No standalone HU payments/acquiring trade association identified; function is distributed across banking, fintech and ICT associations.

why_it_matters: Analysts should not keep searching for a single payments-association register — the equivalent coverage must be assembled from three association member lists plus MNB payment-institution registers (outside this cell).

description: MKIK (Magyar Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara) and BKIK (Budapesti Kereskedelmi és Iparkamara) were in the cell brief as 'Hungarian chambers' but were not searched in this pass; only the American chamber (AmCham) was covered.

result.result_summary: National and Budapest chamber member registers remain unexplored.

why_it_matters: MKIK/BKIK hold a statutory-registration-adjacent company base far larger than any sector association, including small financial intermediaries that no sector association captures.

description: Several association statistics and knowledge-base areas (Lízingszövetség tudásbázis Eurotax/Datahouse categories, HFA riport, Leaseurope statistics) plausibly sit behind member or email gates, but no gate was actually encountered in this pass because the underlying files were not fetched.

result.result_summary: Access status for the deepest data layers of several association sites is unverified — recorded as open with a caveat rather than as blocked.

why_it_matters: Collection design and licensing review depend on whether these are freely redistributable; assuming open access could create a licensing exposure for third-party datasets (Eurotax, Datahouse).

description: Searched in Hungarian for a media-maintained earnings/disclosure calendar ('gyorsjelentés naptár', 'tőzsdei jelentés naptár') that would list upcoming Hungarian bank reporting dates. No trade-press-maintained calendar page was surfaced in this run; earnings dates appear only inside individual preview articles.

result.result_summary: No press-run disclosure calendar identified; date discovery must rely on preview articles ('konszenzus' pieces) or on the primary BSE/issuer disclosure calendars outside this cell.

why_it_matters: Without a calendar, scheduling collection around Hungarian bank reporting dates requires either the exchange's own calendar (different cell) or keyword-triggered monitoring of preview articles.

description: Telex.hu and Növekedés.hu were named in the cell definition, but targeted Hungarian-language searches returned no bank-earnings or IR-event article from either outlet in this run — only the outlets' general descriptions/homepages.

result.result_summary: Both recorded as low-confidence candidates with section-level URLs only; their A1 relevance is unproven, not disproven.

why_it_matters: Prevents overstating coverage; a follow-up site-search pass is needed before either is wired into recurring collection.

description: Portfolio.hu (Signature/premium), hvg.hu (HVG360) and vg.hu are known to gate part of their content, but no fetch in this run measured where the paywall line falls for bank-earnings articles specifically.

result.result_summary: Access status recorded as 'partial paywall' on inference from search snippets, not from a tested fetch.

why_it_matters: Collection design (headline-only vs full-text) depends on how much of the earnings coverage is free; this must be measured before building extractors.

description: All URLs in this slice come from search-result links and inferred section paths. No claim is made that any URL is reachable; several section-level URLs (telex.hu/gazdasag, bbj.hu/finance, bank360.hu, index.hu/gazdasag, napi.hu/magyar-gazdasag, origo.hu/gazdasag) are constructed from observed article paths or brand names.

result.result_summary: URLs supplied with confidence scores only; liveness left to the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Avoids false 'verified' claims and prevents a single failed fetch from being read as a dead source.

description: Targeted hu-language searching for the press rooms of the two dominant Hungarian PSPs — Barion Payment Zrt. and OTP Mobil (SimplePay) — returned only comparison blogs, merchant guides and third-party commentary, no first-party sajtószoba or press-release archive.

result.result_summary: PSP press channels unlocated; only intermediated coverage found for the segment that covers the large majority of HU e-commerce card volume.

why_it_matters: PSP product and partnership announcements are exactly the early weak signals this cell exists to catch; relying on third-party blogs adds latency and editorial distortion.

description: No RSS/Atom feed was observed for any Hungarian bank newsroom in this pass, despite RSS being an explicit part of the cell definition and being searched for in both hu and en.

result.result_summary: Zero confirmed feed endpoints; all candidate newsrooms currently look like HTML-listing crawl targets.

why_it_matters: Without feeds, collection needs polite scheduled HTML crawling with change detection, which is costlier and more brittle — and several sites (Raiffeisen Liferay, BÉT portlets) have unstable URL shapes.

description: Corporate LinkedIn and YouTube newsroom channels for Hungarian banks and PSPs were part of the cell brief but produced no usable results in this pass; no company LinkedIn or YouTube channel URL was observed.

result.result_summary: Social newsroom channel entirely uncovered.

why_it_matters: LinkedIn in particular carries vendor-selection, hiring and go-live posts that never become formal press releases; missing it leaves a systematic blind spot on the earliest signals.

description: MTI OS is a paid publication service; whether its full archive is freely readable and machine-searchable without subscription was not established, only that a public detailed-search page exists.

result.result_summary: Access model of the canonical HU corporate wire remains unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: If OS archive reading is metered, the collection design and budget for the single most important source in this cell change materially.

description: The Budapest Stock Exchange press-room URL returned by search was laden with Spring portlet exception parameters rather than a clean archive path, indicating no stable public permalink was observed for BÉT press releases.

result.result_summary: BÉT press room reachable in principle but no stable entry URL captured.

why_it_matters: BÉT is a statutory disclosure venue; an unstable path risks silent collection failure on a legally significant channel.

description: No EY Hungary (EY Magyarorszag) recurring Hungarian banking-sector survey was found. Searching in Hungarian and English surfaced PwC, KPMG and Deloitte HU financial-sector publications but no EY HU banking-specific annual study page.

result.result_summary: EY appears to be the weakest of the Big4 for publicly indexed Hungarian banking sector research; only global EY banking outlooks are likely to exist for this market.

why_it_matters: The cell assumes four comparable Big4 survey streams; in practice only three are usable for Hungary, so EY should be dropped to a low-frequency manual check rather than a monitored feed.

description: Moody's and Fitch full rating reports and annual Credit Opinions on Hungarian banks are behind registration/subscription walls. This is a hypothesis from their known access model - no fetch was attempted, and nothing here should be recorded as dead.

result.result_summary: Free public layer is limited to headline press releases; the analytical text is gated.

why_it_matters: Automated collection must route through ESMA's European Rating Platform and issuer-republished PDFs (OTP publishes Moody's actions verbatim) instead of scraping the agencies, both for access and for licensing reasons.

description: Several mid-sized Hungarian banks and payment institutions appear to carry no public rating at all (Fitch shows MBH as NR; smaller institutions were not found in any agency listing).

result.result_summary: Rating-agency coverage of the Hungarian banking sector is concentrated on OTP, MBH, the state policy banks (MFB, Eximbank) and the foreign-owned subsidiaries rated on parent support.

why_it_matters: For unrated institutions the only third-party disclosure-grade document is the statutory auditor's report filed on e-beszamolo, which raises the priority of that source relative to the agencies.

description: The Hungarian term 'minositas' is noisy - it also means product quality certification and employee appraisal. 'Hitelminosites' and 'hitelminosito' are the reliable discriminating terms; 'besorolas' works only in combination with an agency name.

result.result_summary: Query design must use hitelminosito / hitelminosites / 'befektetesi ajanlasu besorolas' rather than bare minosites.

why_it_matters: A naive Hungarian keyword feed on 'minosites' will drown the rating-action tripwire in irrelevant hits.

description: Rating agencies themselves publish essentially nothing in Hungarian; Moody's, S&P, Fitch and Scope releases on Hungarian banks are English-only.

result.result_summary: Hungarian-language rating content exists only as (a) issuer disclosures on bank .hu sites and (b) press restatements.

why_it_matters: Local-language coverage for the ratings half of this cell must come from issuers and press, not from the agencies - a structural point for the collection design.

description: No public, enumerable archive of BÉT-hosted 'Kibocsátói Nap' under exactly that name was found. The exchange's issuer-investor event appears under the names 'Kibocsátói Fórum' (e.g. Kibocsátói Fórum 2024), 'Befektetői Klub' and 'BÉT Xmatch' instead.

result.result_summary: Searched the seed term in Hungarian; results resolved to /esemenyek/kibocsatoi-forum-2024 and /esemenyek/befektetoi-klub, not to a 'Kibocsátói Nap' page.

why_it_matters: The seed query's actor name is wrong for this market; downstream collectors keyed on 'kibocsátói nap' would find nothing. The correct HU terms are 'Kibocsátói Fórum', 'Befektetői Klub', 'BÉT Xmatch', 'intézményi befektetői találkozó'.

description: No dedicated OTP-hosted earnings-call webcast/replay page or self-published transcript was located; all located transcripts sit with third-party aggregators (Seeking Alpha, Investing.com, MarketScreener, Yahoo, Quartr).

result.result_summary: OTP's own IR pages surfaced press releases, reports, presentations and an analyst-consensus page, but no transcript or webcast archive in the pages reached.

why_it_matters: Analyst Q&A — the highest-value content in this cell — is therefore only reachable through paywalled or ToS-restricted third parties, creating a legal/access dependency. Worth a targeted follow-up on the EN IR site before assuming it does not exist.

description: Could not confirm active, publicly visible Hungarian bank-sector equity research from KBC Securities Hungária, Random Capital, or a Hungary-specific Raiffeisen Research desk.

result.result_summary: Searches returned no research pages for these entities; only a Raiffeisen Hungary issuer investor presentation and generic KBC corporate references.

why_it_matters: These may be defunct, rebranded, or research-inactive in HU equities. The domestic sell-side map for banks looks concentrated in Concorde, Erste, Equilor and OTP Global Markets, which is itself a finding about market structure.

description: Primary sell-side research output (Concorde, Erste, Equilor, WOOD) is client-gated by design; the full notes are not lawfully collectable.

result.result_summary: Research landing pages are public but note delivery is via client portals or sales contact.

why_it_matters: The workable substitutes are (a) BÉT issuer disclosures of target prices filed by the covered company, (b) issuer-published analyst consensus files, and (c) trade-media reporting. Collection design should centre on those three, not on the brokers' own sites.

description: No public, machine-readable EU-level or third-party mirror was found that specifically archives Hungarian bank INVESTOR-RELATIONS pages as such (as opposed to filings). Archival coverage of retired HU bank IR estates rests on general-purpose web archives (Wayback, OSZK) rather than any finance-specific mirror.

result.result_summary: Searches in HU and EN for archived HU bank IR pages surfaced only general web archives plus the successor bank's own re-hosted sections.

why_it_matters: Historical IR narrative material (presentations, press-release indexes) has no authoritative custodian, so it must be actively harvested and self-archived before it decays.

description: The OSZK Webarchivum's substantive holdings - including the six-monthly national web-space snapshots since 2017 - are not publicly served; only a small share is open, with the rest behind a closed research interface.

result.result_summary: Public documentation states most of the collection is restricted for copyright and privacy reasons; contact route is webarchivum@oszk.hu.

why_it_matters: The most likely alternative archive to Wayback for HU bank sites cannot be used programmatically without a negotiated research access arrangement.

description: Hungary is outside the euro area and the SSM, so the ECB's supervised-entity lists and RIAD do not cover HU-headquartered banks directly; only HU subsidiaries/branches of SSM groups appear. Likewise the EBA transparency exercise sample includes only a small number of HU-linked banks.

result.result_summary: No HU-specific bank list was confirmed inside ECB SSM publications; EBA transparency sample membership per year was not enumerated in this pass.

why_it_matters: Analysts may over-assume EU-level registers give complete HU banking coverage; national MNB/e-beszamolo sources remain indispensable for the domestic-only institutions.

description: The three strongest cross-border normalisation layers for Hungarian bank financials - Orbis Bank Focus, EMIS and D&B/Bisnode - are all subscription products, and none publishes a verifiable Hungary coverage list publicly.

result.result_summary: Product and library pages describe scope generically; no free HU bank coverage manifest found.

why_it_matters: Budget and licensing decisions must be made partly blind; a trial-based coverage test on named HU banks and PSPs is needed before committing.

description: ESAP, the intended EU-wide aggregation of national OAM filings (including MNB Kozzetetelek), is not live; collection is expected to begin July 2026 with publication by 10 July 2027 and phased content additions to 2031.

result.result_summary: Regulation and timelines confirmed; no queryable endpoint exists today.

why_it_matters: Any architecture built now on per-portal crawling should be designed so ESAP can replace several crawlers in 2027 without a rebuild.

description: No established Hungarian-language term was found for 'web archive of investor relations pages' as a service category; Hungarian searching had to fall back on generic 'webarchivum' / 'archiv' plus bank names, which is noisy because 'archiv' on HU bank sites usually labels retired product pages and online-banking notices, not IR history.

result.result_summary: HU queries combining 'befektetoi kapcsolatok' + 'archivum' returned product archives (e.g. investment-fund archives, netbank archives) rather than IR document archives.

why_it_matters: Query design for HU archival discovery must anchor on document nouns (eves jelentes, penzugyi kimutatas, kozzetetel) rather than on 'archivum'.

description: The cell brief lists 'BNP/Cetelem' as a foreign parent reporting Hungary. Search shows Magyar Cetelem Bank Zrt. was sold by BNP Paribas Personal Finance to Cofidis Group (Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale), completed October 2024.

result.result_summary: BNP Paribas is no longer the parent of the Hungarian consumer-credit entity; no current Hungary segment should be expected in BNP's Universal Registration Document for Cetelem. Forward coverage must move to Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale / BFCM investor disclosures and Cofidis Group.

why_it_matters: Continuing to monitor BNP for Hungarian consumer-credit KPIs would yield silence and be misread as a data gap rather than an ownership change.

description: Searched Santander Consumer Finance's consolidated annual accounts and IR pages for a Hungarian entity.

result.result_summary: The geographic operating lists surfaced (Austria, Belgium, Finland, Denmark, Germany, Norway, France, Italy, Netherlands, Switzerland, Poland, UK, Portugal, Spain, China, Canada, Sweden) did not include Hungary. No Santander Consumer Hungary IR disclosure was located.

why_it_matters: Suggests Santander Consumer should be deprioritised or dropped from this cell; the analyst should confirm against the subsidiaries annex of the SCF/Banco Santander annual accounts before writing it off, since search snippets are not an exhaustive perimeter check.

description: Searched in Hungarian for parent-group quarterly reporting on the Hungary segment ('anyabanki negyedéves jelentés', 'Magyarország szegmens eredmény').

result.result_summary: No foreign parent (KBC, Erste Group, RBI, UniCredit SpA, Intesa) publishes its group IR material in Hungarian. Hungarian-language hits were exclusively (a) local subsidiary statutory report pages (kh.hu, raiffeisen.hu) and (b) financial press (Portfolio.hu, Privátbankár.hu) reporting on the foreign releases.

why_it_matters: Local-language monitoring in this cell must target the subsidiary report pages and the press, not the parent IR sites — the parent layer is English-only and should be collected as such.

description: Looked for machine-readable (XLS/XBRL) country-segment data for Hungary from the parents.

result.result_summary: Erste Group publishes annual-report XLS download packs and an ESEF annual financial report, but it was not established from search results whether a Hungary-segment tab/tagging exists. KBC, RBI, UniCredit and Intesa results packages appear to be PDF-first; a KBC 'databook' was referenced only indirectly via analyst-presentation mentions and was not located as a distinct URL.

why_it_matters: Collection design should assume PDF table extraction as the baseline for this cell, with structured data treated as an opportunistic bonus to be verified per issuer.

description: Observed that KBC and RBI host result PDFs on CDN paths containing cache/version tokens (KBC: '.cdn.res/last-modified/{epoch}/'; RBI: '.coredownload.pdf').

result.result_summary: Direct PDF URLs are therefore not durably constructible and may rotate. No fetch was attempted, so none of these are recorded as dead.

why_it_matters: The collector must resolve asset links from the IR index page at collection time rather than templating URLs, or it will accumulate false 404s.

description: Neither the MNB OAM (kozzetetelek.mnb.hu) introduction/documentation nor the e-beszámoló portal documents any public API, RSS feed or bulk export for regulated filings; the OAM introduction page describes only print/save and form-field search.

result.result_summary: Collection from both statutory repositories will require HTML scraping (OAM shows a per-document endpoint pattern /downloadkozzetetel?id=&did=) or, for e-beszámoló, a paid bulk licence.

why_it_matters: Materially raises collection cost and fragility for the two most important sources in this cell; argues for early procurement talks with the e-beszámoló operator and for scraper monitoring on the OAM.

description: The BÉT kibocsátói hírek page as fetched showed no visible RSS/Atom link, pagination controls or archive-depth indicator.

result.result_summary: Archive depth and feed availability for bet.hu issuer announcements are unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: If historical announcements are not deep-linkable, backfill may have to come from the MNB OAM instead, with bet.hu used only for near-real-time monitoring.

description: The Cégközlöny appears under several hostnames in current references — cegkozlony.hu, cegportal.im.gov.hu/frontend/cegkozlony and the older e-cegkozlony.gov.hu — and e-beszámoló returned 404 pages for the legacy path /oldal/kereses_merleglista. Likewise njt.hu and njt.jog.gov.hu both appear live.

result.result_summary: Canonical hosts and stable deep-link paths for the gazette and for some e-beszámoló search endpoints are not settled from search results alone; these are unverified, not dead.

why_it_matters: Collectors keyed on the wrong host or a legacy path will silently break; a deterministic liveness pass must resolve the canonical entry points before build.

description: No Hungarian-language term or portal was found for a consolidated national XBRL/ESEF filing viewer analogous to some other EU OAMs; ESEF filings appear to sit inside the general OAM document store rather than in a dedicated structured-data facility.

result.result_summary: Structured (iXBRL) extraction of HU issuer financials may need per-document handling rather than a national structured feed.

why_it_matters: Affects feasibility of automated financial-line-item extraction for listed HU banks; ESAP may resolve this later.

description: The free e-cégjegyzék company information is explicitly labelled informational ('tájékoztató jellegű') and is refreshed only when registered data change, so the extract's validity date can lag by more than a week.

result.result_summary: Free register data is not suitable as an authoritative point-in-time record.

why_it_matters: Ownership/board changes in payments entities may be detected late; time-critical work should use OCCSZ or Cégközlöny notices instead.

description: No public bulk-download or documented API endpoint was found for the MNB Intézménykereső register (intezmenykereso.mnb.hu). Searches in Hungarian for a downloadable list ('lista letöltés', 'nyilvántartás') returned only licensing-guidance PDFs and the search UI itself.

result.result_summary: Register appears to be a query-only web application; bulk extraction likely requires enumerating its internal XHR endpoints or headless browsing.

why_it_matters: The register is the master actor list for the whole HU run; if it cannot be bulk-extracted, every downstream cell needs a more expensive enumeration strategy or a fallback list source.

description: No MNB-hosted central repository of individual banks' Pillar 3 / nyilvánosságra hozatal reports was found. MNB publishes the disclosure RULES (recommendation 7/2022, superseding 9/2021, plus explanatory tájékoztató), but the actual Pillar 3 PDFs sit on each bank's own website (e.g. UniCredit Bank Hungary, CIB Bank published theirs on their own domains).

result.result_summary: Rules are centralised at MNB; documents are decentralised per institution.

why_it_matters: Pillar 3 collection cannot be solved from this cell — it must be done bank-by-bank in the issuer/IR cells, using the MNB register as the enumeration list and the MNB recommendation as the template schema.

description: Searching Hungarian terms for ICAAP ('tőkemegfelelés belső értékelési folyamata') surfaced only MNB methodological/guidance material and bank risk reports, not any per-institution ICAAP outcome dataset published by MNB.

result.result_summary: ICAAP results are supervisory-confidential; only aggregate capital adequacy appears in the published supervisory tables.

why_it_matters: Sets a realistic ceiling: capital-adequacy comparisons must be built from Aranykönyv/credit-institution tables, not from ICAAP outputs.

description: www.mnb.hu/en/supervision/time-series issued a 307 redirect to statisztika.mnb.hu/statistical-topics/supervisory-statistics, showing that MNB has migrated statistical content between hosts.

result.result_summary: Legacy mnb.hu statistical URLs redirect to the newer statisztika.mnb.hu portal.

why_it_matters: Stored URLs will rot; the pipeline must follow redirects and re-resolve dataset URLs from index pages rather than caching deep links.

description: No Hungarian-language investor-relations or press page was located for Wise's Hungarian presence. Search results indicate Wise Europe SA is registered with the MNB only as a cross-border payment service provider headquartered in Belgium, not as a Hungarian bank or branch, so there appears to be no local filing entity and no HU IR channel. All HU-language material found was tax/accounting commentary about whether Wise HU-IBAN accounts count as domestic payment accounts.

result.result_summary: Hungarian queries returned only advisory/tax content (ado.hu, adozona.hu, fairconto.hu) and a historical FinTechZone piece on TransferWise launching Hungarian account numbers; no corporate disclosure surface.

why_it_matters: Wise is a material player in Hungarian cross-border payments but must be tracked via Wise plc group reporting (UK) and MNB cross-border registers rather than any local disclosure — a structural blind spot if the collection design assumes local filings.

description: Targeted Hungarian-language searching for 'PannonPay' and 'Zen.com' as Hungarian payment institutions returned no corporate, registry, or news evidence tying them to Hungarian licensing or Hungarian filings. I did not find a verifiable Hungarian disclosure surface for either, so I am recording them as unconfirmed rather than inventing a source.

result.result_summary: The combined OR-query surfaced only B-Payment, PayU Hungary, Barion and unrelated entities (BPC Payments Services Zrt., Yettel); nothing for PannonPay or Zen.com.

why_it_matters: Two named cell targets are unverified. They may be dormant, renamed, foreign-passported without local presence, or simply low-profile; a later pass must resolve them via the MNB Intézménykereső by legal name rather than by brand.

description: The seed-brief category 'Netpincér-adjacent PSPs' did not resolve to any identifiable licensed payment institution in Hungarian-language searching. Foodora/Netpincér appears to use third-party gateways rather than operating its own PSP with separate disclosures.

result.result_summary: No Hungarian-language query returned a Netpincér-linked payment institution with its own filings or press channel.

why_it_matters: Marketplace/delivery-embedded payments may therefore be invisible as a standalone disclosure category in HU and must instead be inferred from the gateways' merchant announcements.

description: No Hungarian PSP or EMI in this cell was found to publish a bank-style IR page with periodic results releases. Disclosure is bimodal: statutory audited accounts once a year on e-beszámoló, and irregular marketing-driven press releases or media-relayed claims. Self-reported volume/GMV figures (SimplePay HUF 1,416bn 2022 traffic; B-Payment ~4m monthly transactions; Revolut 2m HU customers) come without audited backing.

result.result_summary: Across all queries, zero quarterly-reporting PSP/EMI IR pages surfaced for Hungary.

why_it_matters: Any collection design must treat issuer volume claims as unaudited assertions and benchmark them against MNB payment statistics; expecting quarterly issuer data will produce empty pipelines.

description: The richest quick-look financial snapshots for these private entities sit behind commercial aggregators (OPTEN, Nemzeti Cégtár, Céginfo, Cégtaláló, Companywall, Dun & Bradstreet) whose terms restrict systematic scraping and redistribution.

result.result_summary: Free tiers expose headline figures (e.g. Barion FY2024 revenue/equity/profit) but full reports and bulk access are paid.

why_it_matters: Systematic collection should route through e-beszámoló (free, statutory, primary) and treat aggregators as manual triage only, or license them explicitly — otherwise the programme takes on legal and continuity risk.

description: No URL in this slice was fetched-and-confirmed by me; all are search-surfaced. Several (e-beszámoló search endpoint, intezmenykereso.mnb.hu, simplepartner.hu download.php) are form/parameter-driven and may behave differently to an automated fetcher than to a browser.

result.result_summary: Confidence scores reflect how strongly the search evidence supports the URL's identity and role, not liveness.

why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass should expect session/JS-dependent behaviour on the registry and filing portals; a non-200 there is a hypothesis of bot defence, not evidence the source is dead.

description: VIBER (Valós Idejű Bruttó Elszámolási Rendszer) has no separate operating company and therefore no standalone annual report. It is operated directly by the MNB, so all VIBER operational and volume disclosure is folded into MNB publications (Fizetési rendszer jelentés, MNB éves jelentés, statisztika.mnb.hu).

result.result_summary: Searched in Hungarian for a VIBER annual report; only MNB-published reports and statistics were found.

why_it_matters: Prevents wasted collection effort hunting for a VIBER corporate report and directs monitoring to the correct MNB endpoints.

description: Posta Elszámoló Központ (PEK) appears to be an internal organisational unit of Magyar Posta Zrt., not a separately reporting legal entity. No independent PEK annual report, website or filing was located in Hungarian searches; the only public description found is a Magyar Posta service page.

result.result_summary: Hungarian searches for 'Posta Elszámoló Központ éves jelentés/beszámoló' returned only Magyar Posta service and terms pages.

why_it_matters: Postal clearing volumes must be sought inside Magyar Posta's consolidated accounts and MNB statistics rather than from a PEK-level source.

description: GIRO Zrt.'s narrative 'éves jelentés' series was observed on the document repository only up to 2023, while the statutory 'éves beszámoló' set runs to 2025. It is unclear whether the narrative report for 2024+ has been discontinued or is simply filed under a different category.

result.result_summary: Repository listing showed éves jelentés 2017-2023 and éves beszámoló 2011-2025.

why_it_matters: If the narrative report has been discontinued, the qualitative scheme-strategy commentary must be replaced by MNB reports and press channels.

description: A targeted search for GIRO Zrt.'s own procurement notices in the Közbeszerzési Értesítő returned only the general procurement framework and unrelated notices; no GIRO-specific tender was surfaced in this pass.

result.result_summary: Search engine did not surface GIRO as a named contracting authority; the gazette's own search interface was not queried directly.

why_it_matters: Whether GIRO publishes tenders as a contracting authority is a load-bearing question for procurement-signal collection and remains unresolved.

description: kozzetetelek.hu was referenced in search-result summaries as an additional statutory publication venue for KELER's annual disclosure data, but the site itself was not fetched or located in this pass; its exact URL and coverage are unconfirmed.

result.result_summary: Mentioned only second-hand in a search summary.

why_it_matters: It may be a useful parallel filing registry; recorded as a lead rather than a source to avoid asserting an unverified endpoint.

description: Searches for a Global Payments / Erste Group joint venture covering Hungary returned only the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Romania JV (announced 2015-07-27, closed 2016-06-01) plus a later Croatian extension. Hungary appears instead as a 2014 outsourcing of Erste Bank Hungary's POS network to Global Payments Europe, not as an equity JV.

result.result_summary: No Hungary-specific Erste/Global Payments JV press release located; Hungarian relationship is an outsourcing/partnership announced Oct 2014 on erstebank.hu.

why_it_matters: The corporate structure determines where Hungarian acquiring revenue is booked and therefore which filing to track; assuming a JV would send collection to the wrong disclosure channel.

description: No dedicated Hungarian-language Mastercard press room (mastercard.hu/sajtokozlemenyek) surfaced; Hungarian Mastercard announcements appear either on the pan-European English newsroom or only via Hungarian trade press (FinTechZone, Privátbankár, vg.hu).

result.result_summary: Hungarian Mastercard PR must be collected indirectly from the European newsroom plus HU trade-press mirrors.

why_it_matters: Creates a dependency on third-party republication, with attribution and completeness risk for scheme-sourced Hungarian statistics.

description: Euronet's recent 10-K names Hungary only as a processing-centre location and reports the EFT Processing segment in aggregate (47,303 ATMs network-wide, ~29% of consolidated revenue in 2023); no Hungary revenue or ATM-count line item was found in the filings surfaced.

result.result_summary: Hungary-level Euronet figures are not in group filings; must be triangulated from the Hungarian statutory accounts and the euronetatms.hu press releases.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic expectations for what the 10-K can and cannot answer, and justifies the e-beszamolo collection path as critical.

description: The Hungarian/English token 'Visa' is heavily polluted by travel-visa content (e.g. Hungary visa requirements pages surfaced in a payments query). Similarly 'Nexi' collides with unrelated brands.

result.result_summary: Scheme-name queries must be constrained with payments terms (kártya, elfogadás, fizetés, bankkártya) or site-scoped to visa.hu.

why_it_matters: Unconstrained scheme-name monitoring will produce a high false-positive rate in any automated collection.

description: No URL in this slice was fetch-verified; all were observed as search-result links only. Worldline's Hungarian media-relations paths in particular are unusually deep and may have rotated.

result.result_summary: All URLs supplied as hypotheses for the deterministic verification pass.

why_it_matters: Deep-path corporate CMS URLs are the most likely to 404 while the section index stays live; verification should fall back to section indexes.

description: Neither Diebold Nixdorf's nor NCR Atleos' public case-study/customer-reference libraries surfaced any Hungary-specific bank case study in hu or en searches; CEE examples found were Czech (CSOB) and German/Nordic.

result.result_summary: Global case-study hubs located and recorded, but no HU-named reference page found.

why_it_matters: The cell's core hypothesis (vendor reference pages expose HU bank decisions) holds only weakly for the two largest ATM OEMs; the stronger HU evidence turned out to be municipal contracts, the MNB ATM regulation and local entity accounts.

description: No Hungarian-language Glory Global Solutions presence (site, distributor page, or HU bank reference) was found for cash recycling / pénzkezelés.

result.result_summary: Only global Glory product and market-share material returned; HU channel unidentified.

why_it_matters: Teller cash recycling in HU branches is likely served through an unnamed distributor; leaves a hole in the branch cash-automation vendor map.

description: The seed-list actor 'Sedlak' could not be resolved to any Hungarian banking/self-service vendor in searches performed; no local-language term for it exists in HU banking vocabulary that I could identify.

result.result_summary: No candidate produced for this seed actor.

why_it_matters: Either the name is a mis-transliteration or the actor is marginal in HU; the seed list should be corrected before the next run.

description: No 4iG announcement about acquiring or entering an ATM / bankautomata business line was found on 4ig.hu or bet.hu disclosure results.

result.result_summary: 4iG's banking-sector exposure is documented only at the IT/integration level in its reports, not as an ATM estate play.

why_it_matters: Prevents an unfounded assumption that 4iG is an ATM channel actor; its relevance is banking-IT integration.

description: Auriga's Hungary exposure appears only via the TRSYS reseller territory list; no named Hungarian bank running WWS was found in hu or en searches.

result.result_summary: Channel identified, end customer not.

why_it_matters: Multivendor ATM software adoption in HU remains unmapped; needs a different route (job ads, tender-free RFI, conference decks).

description: Searched in Hungarian for KAVOSZ Zrt.'s own közérdekű adatok / éves beszámoló pages. kavosz.hu surfaces product hirdetmények and downloadable programme documents, but no dedicated page publishing KAVOSZ Zrt.'s own audited annual accounts was found.

result.result_summary: KAVOSZ statutory accounts must be sourced from the e-beszamolo portal or Nemzeti Cégtár rather than from kavosz.hu.

why_it_matters: Prevents mis-recording KAVOSZ as a self-publishing disclosure source and routes collection to the registry, which is the only dependable channel for it.

description: Hungarian home-savings (lakás-takarékpénztár) searches returned essentially one live actor, Fundamenta-Lakáskassza; no other currently operating home-savings institution with its own annual reporting page was surfaced. Legacy names (Erste Lakástakarék, OTP Lakástakarék) appear only in archived documents.

result.result_summary: The 'other home-savings' part of the cell brief appears to have collapsed to a single reporting entity after the 2018 subsidy withdrawal.

why_it_matters: Scoping expectation for the cell: do not spend collection effort hunting for a plural home-savings segment; monitor Fundamenta plus MNB register diffs instead.

description: Searched in Hungarian for leasing and consumer-finance arms (UniCredit Leasing Hungary, K&H Ingatlanlízing, Erste Lakáslízing, Cofidis) publishing annual reports or Pillar-3 disclosures on their own sites. Results returned only registry/aggregator profiles and business-terms PDFs, no issuer annual-report pages.

result.result_summary: Hungarian pénzügyi vállalkozás subsidiaries generally do not maintain public annual-report pages; their accounts exist only as registry filings and inside the parent bank's consolidated statements.

why_it_matters: Confirms that the leasing/consumer-finance slice of this cell must be collected registry-first (e-beszamolo + MNB Aranykönyv), not issuer-site-first.

description: Search snippets indicate MagNet Bank's public éves jelentések listing may lag by several years (most recent surfaced was 2022) and MTB's konszolidált éves beszámolók archive stops around the 2021 pre-merger period.

result.result_summary: Publication currency for two cell actors is uncertain and could not be confirmed without fetching; recorded as unverified, not as dead.

why_it_matters: Collection design must include a freshness check and a registry fallback rather than assuming issuer pages stay current.

description: English-language searching found MFB and EXIM English annual-report material (plus third-party coverage via Investing.com, Scope Group, NEFI, Devex), but no English disclosure pages for Garantiqa, KAVOSZ, MagNet, Fundamenta or the leasing arms.

result.result_summary: Beyond MFB and EXIM, this cell is effectively Hungarian-only; English-only collection would miss most of it.

why_it_matters: Justifies a hu-first collection pipeline with machine translation, and warns against English-language coverage assumptions for the promotional/specialist segment.
